    WHAT THESE NUMBERS MEAN

    Historical prices.
    Modeled charging choices.

    Dataset 1 gives the energy delivered and the plug-in window. Dataset 2 supplies estimated charger power. The simulation moves charging within that window and checks whether each strategy finishes before unplugging.

    The energy need and unplug deadline are known to each strategy in this replay. The result is a comparison of charging choices, rather than a forecast of a household’s full electricity bill.

    Timers use Oslo time. An arrival within six hours after the scheduled start can charge immediately. Timers and price caps can start earlier, or charge above the cap, when needed to finish before unplugging.

    Data and price basis

    Historical price provenance will appear when the Norway data bundle is loaded.

    Modeled spot-price electricity only. Network fees, tax, VAT, fixed fees, and electricity subsidies are excluded unless the loaded source explicitly says otherwise.

    Before the next-day prices are assumed to be published, SPARC forecasts unknown hours using the previous local day’s matching hour, or the current known price. Final costs use actual historical spot prices.
